name: Embraer Legacy 450/500 / Praetor 500/600
summary: Embraer's fly-by-wire midsize/super-midsize jets with flat-floor stand-up cabins; Flexjet is the dominant US operator.

wings: Low swept wing; Praetor models add tall upswept winglets
engines: Two Honeywell HTF7500E turbofans on pylons high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Straight-sided stand-up cabin with large rounded-rectangle windows
Pointed nose with a large windscreen
tail: T-tail with a strongly swept fin and swept horizontal stabilizer

tellTales: Tall upswept winglets on a midsize twinjet with a T-tail
Long, straight-sided cabin with large rounded windows
Engines on pylons high on the rear fuselage under a sharply swept fin

confusedWith.howToTell: Very hard to separate: the Praetor has more upright winglets and a stubbier tail cone ending close behind the engines, whereas the Challenger 300/350 tapers into a longer tail cone with outward-canted winglets (350/3500).
The Praetor has tall upswept winglets on a slimmer, straight-sided body; the Latitude/Longitude has a fatter, rounder fuselage with plain tips or only small winglets.
The Praetor has rounded-rectangle windows; the G280 has Gulfstream-style oval windows.
The Praetor is a much longer midsize jet with more windows; the Phenom 300 is a short light jet.
